sources.excerpt: Fuzzrocious Pedals and Electronic Audio Experiments Release Wicked Jawn Pedal – No Treble Skip to main content No Treble Gear Basses Amps Pedals & Effects Accessories & Strings Pickups Bass of the Week Gear Reviews News New Albums Sheet Music & Instruction Concerts & Tours Events Columns From the Bottom Bass Players To Know Ask Damian Erskine Recording Bass The Lightbulb Moment The Lowdown with Dr. D Health & Fitness Lessons Keep It Groovy Bass Gym Talking Technique Bass Transcriptions The Brown’stone Creative Bass Lines Bass & Creativity Bass Lick Series Advanced Bass Talking Style Bassists Interviews Wonder Women Stories Behind the Songs Reader Spotlight In Memoriam Share Your Story Videos Podcast Bass Nerds Podcast Groove Podcast Shop Subscribe Archives On This Day in Bass Contributors Contact Home Bass Gear Pedals & Effects Fuzzrocious Pedals and Electronic Audio Experiments Release Wicked Jawn Pedal by Kevin Johnson Sunday, September 1st, 2019 Share Tweet Email Comments Fuzzrocious Pedals and Electronic Audio Experiments have teamed up for their first collaboration. The resulting pedal is called the Wicked Jawn, which includes slang from each of the builders’ local cities. “Both Boston and Philadelphia have distinct accents and colloquial expressions. Bostonians are known for saying ‘wicked’ and Philadelphians for ‘jawn,'” the Fuzzrocious site explains. “Both are baseball cities. We’ve combined circuits, colors/fonts from our local ball squads, and nerd brains to bring you something special!” The new pedal combines the Electronic Audio Experiments Model FET preamp (based on the Sunn Model T) with the Fuzzrocious Octave Jawn, which is a digital octave up and down circuit. Each side can be toggled on and off with independent footswitches. Check out this demo (bass starts at 1:15): The Fuzzrocious Pedals & Electronic Audio Experiments Wicked Jawn is available in limited numbers with a direct price of $285. Fuzzrocious Pedals/Electronic Audio Experiments Wicked Jawn Pedal Features: Independent Footswitches Digital Octave Up/Down with Mix Knob Independent gain controls for the Normal and Brite channels 3-band FMV EQ Master volume In his time with No Treble, Kevin has met hundreds of amazing bassists and interviewed icons like Jack Casady, Victor Wooten, Les Claypool, Marcus Miller, and more. He's a gigging bassist performing jazz in Northern Virginia and bluegrass with The Plate Scrapers up and down the East Coast. Kevin appreciates all genres of music, from R&B to metal and everything in between. Connect with Kevin on Facebook and check his performance schedule on his website .
